description: A lambda captures the scope it was written in, not the scope it is called from.

tests.input: adder(n) := (x -> x + n); add5 := adder(5); add5(3)
tests.notes: The captured value is the parameter of the enclosing call
The lambda captured a as it was when it was written, so the later change is not seen
A named function is not a closure: it looks a up when it runs, so it sees 2

tests.input: adder(n) := (x -> x + n); a := adder(1); b := adder(100); a(0) + b(0)
tests.notes: Each call captures its own binding rather than sharing one
